method_notes: TASK 1 (identity). For each of the seven flagged official_url values I first re-fetched the bad URL myself rather than trusting the census note, then researched the ground's current occupant, then fetched each candidate replacement and required it to identify THIS GROUND (address, ground name, or explicit statement of where the club plays) - not merely to carry a similar club name. Five replacements met that bar; two did not and are left as OFFICIAL_URL_REVIEW_REQUIRED with the reason recorded. Every bad URL is preserved in invalid_official_url with what it actually served on 2026-09-20. TASK 2 (no-calendar recovery). The 106-venue list was derived programmatically: venues.json venue_census_ids absent from every record in calendar-sources.json (642 venues, 730 sources, 106 with no source - matches the brief). Segmentation: A = principal capacity (capacity-evidence.json, is_principal true) of 5,000 or more, or a nationally significant arena/complex; B = a sport venue with an expected fixture source (greyhound tracks, a racecourse, and senior national-league football grounds); C = conference/exhibition and major public-programme cultural venues with an expected event calendar (I extended C beyond strict conference/exhibition to cover the concert hall and theatre in the list, which belong to the same "expected published programme" tier); D = smaller >=1,000-capacity grounds with a weak public programme, mostly Scottish junior and Northern Irish intermediate football, which were deliberately NOT worked. The 106 split A 22 / B 37 / C 5 / D 42. ATTEMPTED: A 22 of 22, B 37 of 37, C 5 of 5, D 0 of 42 - D was deliberately left, per the brief. Segment A was worked in descending principal-capacity order from 25,849 downward. Verification rule applied throughout: a source was only recorded after I fetched it and saw either the venue/club identified on the page or dated event content. events_currently_present is true only where I saw named forthcoming dated events; where the page is the right one but renders nothing to a plain fetch, or the season has ended, it is false and the note says which. Several rugby league club pages are legitimately empty on 2026-09-20 because the 2026 season has just finished - that is recorded as a season state, not as an absent calendar. Sources NOT used: ticket marketplaces, aggregator fixture sites, and any domain I could not fetch. Three further squatted or dead domains were found and are recorded as negative findings so they are never adopted: manchestersportandleisure.org (gambling spam), eastbournetennis.com (redirects to a slot site), penybontfc.com (redirects to slot spam) - plus dead/placeholder official_urls at stdavidshallcardiff.co.uk (no DNS), pitchero.com/clubs/merthyrtown (Pitchero "Club not live"), and cpfc.co.uk/palace-women recorded against Gander Green Lane. Tooling note: WebSearch quota was exhausted partway through, after which discovery used the DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint and the Wikipedia search API, with all confirmation still done by direct fetch. Cloudflare-protected sites (leicestertigers.com, mancity.com) were read in a real browser. Sites with TLS faults (theatreroyal.co.uk expired certificate, downpatrickracecourse.co.uk incomplete chain, whitehavenrl.co.uk apex handshake failure, brechincity.co.uk SSL alert 80) are recorded with the exact fault.
